items.title: fix(identity): keep private keys and password-derived hashes out of auth logs (#6181)
items.body: ## Summary Fixes the remaining live half of #6181 on current main. The SSH (`cmd/ssh`) and web (`web`) surfaces were already cleaned and carry AST guard tests; the transitive helper package the SSH path calls — `pkgs/identity/auth` — still wrote credential material to the log: - `InsertPrivateKey` logged the base64-encoded **ed25519 private key** (`privateKeyString`) in three places. - `InsertHashPublicKey` / `GetPublicKeyFromHash` logged the **password-derived SHA-256 hash** (`hash`) — a replayable password equivalent in this scheme, since the hash is what the gateway looks keys up by. - `InsertTextPublicKey` / `GetPublicKeyFromText` / `GetPublicKey` logged the same derived value as `text`. This is exactly the scope gap task 10653 was blocked on in 2026-11-06; its preserved WIP branch no longer exists, so the fix was redone against current main. ## Changes - `pkgs/identity/auth/auth.go`: the seven log calls above now emit only non-secret metadata (key type, hash/text type, public key string, ids, rows affected). Private-key material and password-derived values no longer reach any log record. Storage behavior is unchanged — the values are still written to the DB, just never logged. - `pkgs/identity/auth/auth_logging_test.go` (new): AST guard mirroring the existing `cmd/ssh` and `web` suites — fails if a logger call in the six credential-handling functions references `pk`, `privateKeyString`, `hash`, `text`, or `password`, or a field of those names. ## Tests - `go test ./auth ./web ./cmd/ssh` — all pass, including the new guard. - `go build ./...` for the identity module fails in a pre-existing, unrelated place (the charm fork's module-cache copy references undefined migration symbols); the three affected packages build and test clean. Closes #6181 (with the already-landed ssh/web halves). --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Authentication logs no longer include private-key material or supplied hash and text values. Public-key logging now reports only the public-key type and representation.
